title.en: Reporting passives and have/get something done
title.es: Pasivas de información y have/get something done

summary.en: To report what people believe or say without naming them, use **It is said that…** or **He is said to…**. To talk about services or things that happen to us, use **have/get + object + past participle**: _I had my hair cut_, _She's getting the car repaired_. Both structures put the focus on the result, not on the doer.
summary.es: Equivale a «se dice que…» o «se cree que…» (reporting passive) y a «me corté el pelo» cuando otra persona lo hace (causative). En español usamos la forma reflexiva; en inglés es **have + objeto + participio**: no se dice *I cut my hair* si lo hace el peluquero.

form: **Subject + is/was + said/thought/believed + to + infinitive** (_He is said to be ill._)
Earlier events: **to have + past participle** (_She is believed to have left._)
Ongoing situations: **to be + -ing** (_The company is reported to be losing money._)
Causative: **have/get + object + past participle** (_We had the roof repaired._)
**Get** is more informal and often suggests something happened to you: _He got his phone stolen._

uses.text: **Reporting general opinion**: _It is thought that the strike will end soon._
**Same idea with a personal subject**: _The strike is thought to end soon._
**Looking back**: _The painting is believed to have been stolen in 1998._

note.en: Use to have + past participle when the reported event is earlier than the reporting verb.
note.es: Si el hecho es anterior al verbo de información, usa to have + participio.

uses.text: **Arranging a service**: _I'm having my kitchen painted next week._
**Unwelcome experiences**: _She had her bag stolen on the train._

note.en: The same pattern can describe something bad that happens to you, not something you arranged.
note.es: El mismo patrón sirve para algo malo que te ocurre: had her bag stolen.

mistakes.wrong: I cut my hair at the salon every six weeks.
mistakes.right: I have my hair cut at the salon every six weeks.

why.en: If someone else does the job for you, use have + object + past participle.
why.es: Si lo hace otra persona, usa have + objeto + participio; I cut my hair significa que lo haces tú.

mistakes.wrong: He is said that he is a millionaire.
mistakes.right: He is said to be a millionaire.

why.en: With a personal subject, the reporting passive is followed by to + infinitive, not a that-clause.
why.es: Con sujeto personal: is said to be, no is said that.

mistakes.wrong: They are said to leave the country last year.
mistakes.right: They are said to have left the country last year.

why.en: For an earlier event, use the perfect infinitive.
why.es: Para un hecho pasado: to have left.

mistakes.wrong: I had repaired my car yesterday.
mistakes.right: I had my car repaired yesterday.

why.en: The causative order is have + object + past participle. The past perfect has a different meaning.
why.es: El orden es have + coche + participio; I had repaired es past perfect.

examples.en: It is said that the old mill is haunted.
examples.es: Se dice que el viejo molino está encantado.

examples.en: The minister is believed to have resigned last night.
examples.es: Se cree que el ministro dimitió anoche.

examples.en: I'm having my passport renewed this month.
examples.es: Este mes me van a renovar el pasaporte.

examples.en: The factory is reported to be closing next year.
It was widely believed that the economy would recover.
She had her car broken into while she was shopping.
We're getting the boiler serviced on Thursday.
The suspect is thought to be living abroad.
Have you ever had your portrait painted?
He's had his teeth whitened, and it shows.

practice.prompt: The new tunnel ___ to be the longest in the country.

explanation.en: The reporting passive is is said to + infinitive.

practice.prompt: We ___ the windows replaced next week.

explanation.en: Someone else will do the work, so use have + object + past participle.

practice.prompt: The thieves are believed ___ the country before the alarm went off.

explanation.en: The leaving happened before the belief is reported, so use the perfect infinitive.

practice.prompt: I need to ___ my laptop looked at; it keeps crashing.

explanation.en: Get + object + past participle is a causative pattern; make and do do not work here.
